name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti
memory_bandwidth_basis: GDDR6X 21 Gbps data rate x 384-bit / 8 = 1008 GB/s (NVIDIA Ada whitepaper, 'Memory Clock (Data Rate) 21 Gbps', 'Memory Bandwidth 1008 GB/sec')
notes:
10752 CUDA cores, 1.86 GHz boost / 1.56 GHz base, 450 W TGP, PCIe Gen4. This is the only GeForce in this set with NVLink (the 3090 family's NVLink bridge is shown on the product page), so 2-way SLI was the only consumer multi-GPU path on Ampere.

Same 24 GB GDDR6X capacity as the non-Ti 3090 but a faster memory part (21 vs 19.5 Gbps => 1008 vs 936 GB/s). Batch-1 decode is memory-bound, so this bandwidth delta is the mechanical reason the Ti decodes tokens faster at identical VRAM capacity.

FP8/INT8/INT4 tensor figures not recorded: not verified against a primary source in this pass.
